title: Client-visible pin resolution, cryptographic lock proofs, and rollback-safe pinning API
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Implement a clear, client-observable pinning API that produces a verifiable 'lock proof' and integrates published performance profiles at the pinned version. The goal is to give SDK clients deterministic resolution, a compact signed artifact they can persist (a lockfile), and safe rollback semantics for canary/gradual rollouts. This ticket covers API surface design, server-side resolution guarantees, lock proof format, and runtime changes to emit the proof with responses and console artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: SDK can call /resolve?pin=... and receive a deterministic resolution chain (provider tag -> semver -> commit-hash) in a stable, documented JSON format
Server produces a signed lock proof (base64) that includes resolved model ref, model_digest (commit hash), published performance_profile_id, timestamp, and resolver_version
Clients can persist the lock proof and later re-validate the currently-served model against it; mismatch detection returns structured error codes
Console and SDK tooling expose performance_profile metadata tied to the resolved model and surface quantization/throughput recommendations
Rollback flow: creating a new pin with a 'rollback-safe' flag initiates a staged rollback policy with retention of previous lock proofs and an automatic alert to the owning team
Integration tests that simulate alias-fast-forward, tag reassignment, and semver range resolution are added and pass in CI
spec: API endpoints: 1) POST /pins/resolve {pin: string, client_id?: string} returns fields: resolved_ref, model_digest, performance_profile_id, resolution_graph (ordered list of steps), lock_proof (signed_base64), resolver_version. 2) GET /pins/lockfile/:id returns canonical lockfile for persistence. Lock proof format: JSON string signed with platform key, fields: {resolved_ref, model_digest, perf_profile, created_at, resolver_version, ttl_seconds, signature_version}. Signature: RSA-PSS over canonical JSON; clients validate via platform public key. Resolution semantics: pin accepts tag, semver range, commit hash; resolution must be monotonic per resolver_version and documented fallbacks prioritized as: exact hash > tag exact match > semver exact match > semver range latest compatible. When a tag or semver resolves to a different commit than a previously-obtained lock_proof, server returns a resolution_conflict code and emits an audit event. Performance profiles are immutable artifacts published with model_digest; when publishing a profile, runtime validates compatibility matrix (sequence_length, quantization_profile), and publishes recommendations to the profile object. Backwards compatibility: prior 'pin' shorthand continues to resolve as before but will now also provide lock proofs when requested. Rollback safety: pins can be created with metadata {rollback_safe: true, retained_lockproofs: n}; creating such a pin triggers retention of n previous lock proofs and ties into rollout policies in Console for one-click revert.
technical_approach: Server-side resolver will be extended to return an ordered resolution_graph and to compute a deterministic model_digest for any non-hash selector by reading the model registry's canonical commit mapping. We will add a signer service (signer-readonly endpoint) that signs canonical lock proof JSON. SDKs will get a new 'resolve' call and helpers to persist/validate lock proofs. The runtime will accept an optional header X-Expect-Lock-Proof and attach lock_proof to streaming responses for the first chunk. To avoid latency impact, signer runs asynchronously but must be returned before the resolve call completes; signer is replicated and highly-available. Auditing will write resolution events to the existing audit log pipeline with additional fields for lock_proof_id and resolver_version. For rollback, Console will call a new pins/rollback endpoint which references retained lock proofs and wires into the rollout controller. We'll gate the signer behind a feature flag and enable gradual rollout to early customers.
implementation_notes: Add signer microservice: minimal dependencies, key rotation plan, public-key endpoint for SDKs
Extend model registry API with GET canonical_digest_for(selector) to support deterministic resolution
Add resolve endpoint to API gateway with enriched response shape; update API contract docs
SDK changes: add resolve() helper, Lockfile client that can persist and validate lock proofs; add validation error types
Console changes: display lock_proof_id, show perf_profile recommendations, and add one-click rollback using retained proofs
Instrument audit logs and billing metadata to include perf_profile ids used per request
test_plan: Unit tests for resolver priority rules and canonicalization
Integration tests: tag reassignment scenario where tag moves to new commit after client persisted a lock proof; client should observe mismatch and emit RESOLUTION_MISMATCH

End-to-end test: publish performance profile for digest X, resolve pin that maps to X, confirm SDK receives perf_profile_id and runtime enforces suggested batch/quantization settings in a staging runtime
Security test: verify signature validation of lock_proof using rotated keys; simulate key rotation and verify old proofs remain verifiable if within TTL
Fault injection: signer delayed/unavailable -> resolve still returns best-effort fields and a clear code to clients; rollouts blocked if signer unavailable and rollback_safe requested
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the signer + resolve response. Phase 1: internal dogfood for Redwood teams (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta customers via console toggle (4 weeks). Phase 3: default-on for new pins and opt-out for legacy pins (2 weeks). Monitor: resolution mismatch rate, signer latency p95, number of rollbacks initiated. Have rollback SOP if signer key mis-signs; key rotation must be coordinated with support.
